title: Arjuna asks where to see Krishna

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचपरं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् । पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: You are the supreme reality, the highest refuge, the purest one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading.
verses.angle: Arjuna names Krishna as supreme reality
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen Krishna as the source of all creation. Now he answers with a string of names. Listen to what each title means.

body.text: Arjuna says: You are the supreme reality, the highest refuge, the purest one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading. Arjuna names Krishna the supreme reality and the highest refuge, the pure one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading. He then adds that all the sages, including Narada and Vyasa, speak of Krishna this way.

verses.sa: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा । असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥
verses.tr: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me.
verses.angle: Sages and Krishna speak the same truth
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna lists the great sages who speak of Krishna this way, and then adds Krishna himself to their number.

body.text: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me. The verse names sages like Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, and then adds Krishna himself to their number. Arjuna then accepts all of this as true, saying that even the gods do not know your full form.

verses.sa: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव । न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥
verses.tr: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form.
verses.angle: Keshava: the Lord whom even gods do not know
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is listening to Krishna describe his divine nature, and he tells Krishna to listen for the one thing that makes this truth so staggering.

body.text: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form. Arjuna calls Krishna Keshava, and he says he accepts every word as true, yet he admits that neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form. He now says that only the Supreme Person can know himself, setting up the next verse.

verses.sa: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम । भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥
verses.tr: O Supreme Person, you alone know yourself by yourself, O source of all beings, lord of all beings, divine of the divine, ruler of the world.
verses.angle: Svayameva: Krishna knows his own self
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just accepted Krishna as the divine source behind all existence. Now he acknowledges a truth about Krishna's nature and speaks it aloud.

body.text: O Supreme Person, you alone know yourself by yourself, O source of all beings, lord of all beings, divine of the divine, ruler of the world. Arjuna says that you alone know your own self by your own self. This shows that Krishna is not dependent on anyone else to know who he is, and he is the source of all beings. Arjuna asks Krishna to fully describe his divine manifestations, by which he pervades and sustains all the worlds.

verses.sa: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥
verses.tr: Only you can fully describe your own divine manifestations, by which you pervade and sustain all these worlds.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just called Krishna the source of all beings, and now he asks for the details of that source.

body.text: Only you can fully describe your own divine manifestations, by which you pervade and sustain all these worlds. The word tvam, you, shows Krishna filling and sustaining all these worlds through these divine manifestations. Arjuna then asks how to fix his mind on these forms through constant contemplation.

verses.sa: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् । केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥
verses.tr: O Yogi, how shall I know You by constant contemplation? In what forms should You be contemplated, O Blessed One?
verses.angle: Devotion needs a form the mind can return to again and again.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has moved from fear to deep reverence, and now he asks for a practical path. Listen for the exact forms he wants to hold in his mind.

body.text: O Yogi, how shall I know You by constant contemplation? In what forms should You be contemplated, O Blessed One? Arjuna asks how to know Krishna by constant contemplation, and wants to know in which forms he should be contemplated. He wants a concrete anchor for his mind. He asks for a clear way to keep Krishna in his thoughts at all times.

verses.sa: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन । भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥
verses.tr: O Janardana, tell me again in detail of Your yogic power and Your manifestations, for I am not satisfied hearing Your nectar-like words.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has stopped asking about war and now asks about Krishna himself. He says he cannot hear enough.

body.text: O Janardana, tell me again in detail of Your yogic power and Your manifestations, for I am not satisfied hearing Your nectar-like words. Arjuna calls Krishna's words nectar and says he is not satisfied hearing them. He is turning devotion into a hunger to know the divine more fully. Krishna agrees to speak, saying there is no end to His divine expansions.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचहन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार.
verses.angle: anantah: endless, the limit of language
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna starts to answer. Listen for one word that tells you why he can only give a partial list.

body.text: Krishna says: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार. Listen for anantah, endless. Krishna says there is no end to his manifestations, so he can only name the main ones, because a full list is impossible. He then says he is the Self seated in every heart, the beginning, middle and end of all beings.

verses.sa: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
verses.tr: I am the Self, O Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.
verses.angle: ahama: the Self present at beginning and end
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asked to know Krishna’s divine forms, and Krishna replies that he is closest of all: he is the Self inside every heart. Listen to how he names the three stages of existence.

body.text: I am the Self, O Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings. Listen to the word ahama, I am, repeated at the start and again before the end of beings. It shows the same speaker, the same Self, is present at the very start and the very finish of every life. Krishna then names a new pair of opposites, the sun and the moon, among the sons of Aditi.

verses.sa: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् । मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥
verses.tr: Among the sons of Aditi, I am Vishnu; among radiant things, I am the sun with rays. I am the brilliance in the Maruts, and among stars, I am the moon.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues naming the bright powers of the world. Listen for how he places himself among the lights.

body.text: Among the sons of Aditi, I am Vishnu; among radiant things, I am the sun with rays. I am the brilliance in the Maruts, and among stars, I am the moon. The verse tells us that Vishnu is among the sons of Aditi, and that the sun is among radiant things. By choosing the brightest of each group, Krishna shows that the great powers of the world are simply different forms of his presence. Krishna moves from cosmic lights to the gods, saying he is the Sama Veda among the Vedas and Indra among the radiant beings.

verses.sa: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः । इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥
verses.tr: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the radiant beings, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind; among living beings, I am consciousness.
verses.angle: Asmi: the repeated claim of identity
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers a question with four names. Listen for the single thread that binds them all.

body.text: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the radiant beings, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind; among living beings, I am consciousness. The word asmi, I am, repeats four times, binding each object to the speaker. The verse places the mind above the senses and names it as the ruling presence among them. He now names the Rudras and Kubera, moving from the inner world of the mind to the outer world of the gods.

verses.sa: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् । वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥
verses.tr: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am fire, and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru.
verses.angle: Kubera, the lord of wealth among the Yakshas and Rakshasas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The battlefield falls silent as Krishna describes the greatest of each group he represents.

body.text: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am fire, and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru. Shankara is the greatest among the fierce Rudras, Kubera is the lord of wealth among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, and Meru is the highest of all mountain peaks, showing Krishna is the greatest of each group. Krishna moves on to the greatest of priests, commanders, and waters, to show his presence in leadership and depth.

verses.sa: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् । सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
verses.tr: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for one name among commanders. Krishna is naming the greatest powers of the world, and one name here stands out as the peak of military strength.

body.text: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean. Skanda, the name Krishna uses for himself among commanders, is the name of the god of war, pointing to supreme martial strength. Next, Krishna turns from human and divine power to the vastness of the ocean and the syllable Om.

verses.sa: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् । यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥
verses.tr: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one imperishable syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the steadfast I am the Himalayas.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his list of divine presences, naming the most revered forms across the world. Listen to the specific names he chooses.

body.text: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one imperishable syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the steadfast I am the Himalayas. Krishna names Bhrigu the greatest of sages and the Himalayas the most steadfast of mountains. He also picks the one imperishable syllable and the sacrifice of silent repetition, showing his presence in the quietest and most enduring things. He continues the list with the sacred fig tree, Narada, Chitraratha, and Kapila. The roll call goes on.
